log.limits: Courts of Indian Offenses: 25 C.F.R. § 11.100 no longer lists courts (since 85 FR 645, 2020); it points to the Bureau of Indian Affairs website, so the current list was taken from https://www.bia.gov/CFRCourts (16 nations; the Santa Fe and Albuquerque Indian School properties held for the 19 Pueblos are not a single nation and were not recorded). Tribal Law and Policy Institute directory (justice.htm) is dated (server Last-Modified 2022-07-06, entries older); links were not re-checked; Courts of Indian Offenses mentions in it were dropped in favor of the Bureau of Indian Affairs list; intertribal courts and consortia (Association of Village Council Presidents, Intertribal Court of Northern/Southern California, Northern California Tribal Courts Coalition) were not attributed to member nations. The joint Shoshone and Arapaho entry was not split between the two Wind River nations. Healing-to-wellness courts: wellnesscourts.org loads its state lists through a site AJAX endpoint that I did not call (blocked by my permission settings), and its grantee and mentor court pages are password-protected, so healing-to-wellness coverage is minimal (one law-named wellness court). National Indian Law Library pages carry no update dates; facts from them use the access date as as_of. Pages that say 'None available', or that only point to Westlaw or the library catalog, produced no governing-document fact. Westlaw and catalog links were not recorded. Constitution and code titles come from the library's table-of-contents page headings where fetched, otherwise a generic title ('Constitution', 'Tribal code') with the page wording kept in the note. Dispute-resolution provisions: the 46 Native American Rights Fund entries were not read, so no summary sentence was written (the organization's own description is in the note). Provisions found in National Indian Law Library code tables of contents are identified by heading only. Tribal codes that are not on the library's site were not searched for dispute-resolution provisions. Government structure: recorded only where a document or table states the act: historical constitutions transcribed by the University of Oklahoma Law Library (statute cited in preamble, approval or certification) and Haas (1947) Table B. Both are historical; many nations have since adopted new or amended constitutions, so these say how the constitution was adopted at that time, not necessarily the current document. Alaska villages whose text cites only the 1934 act are recorded as the Alaska amendment (explained in note). Name matches by former name (Papago, Devil's Lake Sioux, Fort McDowell Mohave-Apache, Upper Lake Band, Sisseton-Wahpeton Sioux, Ketchikan Indian Corporation) are low confidence. Covelo Indian Community and 'Rule River Indian Tribe' (Haas) were not matched. Component reservations of the Minnesota Chippewa Tribe (Bois Forte, Fond du Lac, Grand Portage, Leech Lake, Mille Lacs, White Earth) and constituent bands of the Paiute Indian Tribe of Utah are recorded under the federally listed entity, with the band named in the note. No Native Hawaiian, state-recognized or other non-federal groups were added (National Indian Law Library lists a few state-recognized and unrecognized groups; skipped). Names with diacritics were kept as the sources give them. National Indian Law Library coverage: 596 index pages fetched; for 126 matched pages the page listed nothing usable (only 'None available', the library catalog or Westlaw), so they produced no facts and their page sources were dropped from the sources list. 195 constitution and 182 code table-of-contents pages were fetched; 79 of them had headings matching peacemaking, mediation, arbitration, dispute resolution, family group conference, talking circle or restorative justice, grouped into one fact per heading block. Many arbitration and 'dispute resolution' hits are gaming patron-dispute, employment or contract provisions rather than general civil dispute resolution; kind 'other' marks generic 'dispute resolution' headings.
log.narrative: Bulk-first method. (1) Read 25 C.F.R. § 11.100 through the eCFR API and the 2020 Federal Register rule that moved the list to the Bureau of Indian Affairs website; took the current list from bia.gov/CFRCourts. (2) Parsed the Tribal Law and Policy Institute 'Justice Systems of Indian Nations' directory into court names and linked constitutions/codes. (3) Fetched all 596 National Indian Law Library per-nation pages (1 request per second) and parsed the Tribal Code, Tribal Constitution and Contact Info blocks; then fetched the library's constitution and code table-of-contents pages to get exact titles, ratification/revision dates, and to search headings for peacemaking, mediation, arbitration and related terms. (4) Parsed the Native American Rights Fund Indigenous Peacemaking Initiative law lists (general, youth and family, other materials). (5) For government structure, fetched the University of Oklahoma Law Library collection of IRA-era constitutions and charters (351 files, including 6 PDFs) and classified each constitution by the statute it cites; added Haas (1947) Table B (main, Oklahoma, Alaska). Names were matched to roster ids by exact normalized name, then by distinctive-token overlap; every non-exact match was reviewed by hand and corrected where wrong (for example Wilton Rancheria, Gila River).
